its definitely not trivial to offer *any* kind of privacy as a perp dex, no matter the design. incomplete things to get right:
- privacy from the sequencer
- privacy from the prover
- post-trade privacy
- orderbooks under privacy
- ticker tape under privacy
- liquidations under privacy
- any type of observable fairness/integrity under privacy

these are in fundamental friction with each other and lighter is no closer to solving any of them than HL or anyone else. its not even clear they can be solved.

tweets.text:
There is a fundamental problem in the logic that AI will make companies more competitive - that is not a good thing

Competition means profits being competed away

Any company that can use AI to reduce cost also means every other company can reduce cost and ultimately it causes margin compression

AI is not helping companies create moats - its commoditisation of the moats they once had 

Those intelligent lawyers, accountants, engineers were previously talent moats with scarcity

This is like the 2 parent working household - at the start it seems like a boom with more income but overtime that becomes the new baseline for affordability

AI is only driving more extreme competition and it will only make it harder for every business not easier when it comes to winning

The goal of a business is not lowering costs or having less employees - its long term profitability

tweets.text:
History rhymes but doesnt repeat is a great way to think about whats happening in AI 

The reason people are confident and piling into AI is they can see that unlike the tech bubble there is mass adoption of AI models in real time - so its said this is different to speculation of 2000s

However what this does is it makes people think that as long as there is fundamentals that the valuations make sense

This is the new rhyming lesson - that fundamentals dont mean valuations are justified

Hence rather than a bubble its more like a boom and bust

Imagine a restaurant making no money valued at 1m - thats the tech bubble. Today is a restaurant making 1m a year except the valuation is 100m. Yes its better than tech bubble in underlying and yes its a business with revenue but that doesnt mean the valuations make sense

tweets.text:
When talking about AI frontier lab companies I believe people are making the same mistake as they did with altcoins in the long term   

X is value created and Y is the ability to capture a percentage of X  

Just because something is very valuable to people in use doesn’t mean you deserve a high valuation- you have to be able to maintain and extract margins over time while growing

Similarly the AI hardware companies are eventually the computer companies of yesteryear - they will trend to perfect competition especially when China catches up

Frontier labs are basically selling dollars for pennies but unlike Amazon that ran a loss for years etc Amazon had option to turn profitable they just decided to keep investing - these companies have no path to doing that. Their costs are scaling linearly with the revenue - meaning they are not seeing economies of scale
